current_example.title: Example: Finding the Square Root of a Negative Number Squared

q-40870.name: Question 1
q-40870.worked_solution:
The number in the square root is non-negative, so the square and the square root cancel each other out.

Therefore, we have

$$
(\sqrt{16})^{2}=16.
$$

q-71564.name: Question 3
q-71564.worked_solution:
Remember that by definition, the square root is always zero or positive, never negative.

So, the square root comes out to

$$
\sqrt{(-100)^{2}}=\sqrt{{100}^{2}}=100.
$$

q-71564.html:
Question 3
?

What is (−100)2?

a
Not a real number
b
100
c
±10
d
−100
e
10
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Remember that by definition, the square root is always zero or positive, never negative.

So, the square root comes out to

(−100)2=1002=100.
